content:
Priya: Drafting a short RFC follow-up — propose a lightweight "quant-shim" between model artifacts and runtime. Purpose: normalize FP8/INT8/4bit metadata, provide fallback hooks, and allow gradual deprecation of awkward per-model hacks.

Evan: +1. Can you sketch the API surface? Where does shim live — build time, load time, or request-time?

Priya: Load-time primarily. Shim converts model metadata into a canonical "precision profile" that runtime can consume. Minimal runtime changes: accept profile + fallback sequence. Example profile snippet:
```
precision_profile:
  preferred: fp8
  fallbacks: [int8, 4bit]
  per_layer_overrides: {attn:q: int8}
  degradation_budget: 0.02
```

Lina: How do we measure degradation_budget? unit is relative perplexity or task-specific metric?

Priya: Good q — default is calibration delta on heldout prompt set (mean token-level score). Ops teams can attach customer-specific evals for stricter thresholds.

Marco: Edgecase: what if fp8 produces NaNs in some layers at runtime? Shim should detect and fast-fallback to safe variant without dropping the whole request.

Priya: Exactly — shim exposes fast probe: before committing to fp8 path, runtime runs a cheap layer-sanity check (e.g., single forward of a short sentinel prompt using streaming harness). If check fails, fallback to next tier. That keeps p99 latency tight.

Evan: Sounds runtime-heavy. Can we cache probe results per model+hardware+seed for X minutes to avoid extra cost?

Priya: Yes — caching + TTL. Also telemetry: probe_failures counter, fallback_rate, per-layer-NaN counts.

ops-bot: FYI: Any config changes must be toggleable via feature-flag + rollout. Ops prefers "quant_shim.enabled" default true for canary hosts only.

Marco: Migration plan idea:
- Phase 0: shim as read-only translator for existing profiles (no fallbacks).
- Phase 1: enable fallbacks + probes on canary group (~5%).
- Phase 2: rollout to dedicated pools with telemetry SLO gates.
- Phase 3: deprecate per-model ad-hoc logic, enforce profile lint.

Lina: What about storage format for profiles? JSON? protobuf?

Priya: Use compact protobuf on disk (v2) for speed, but SDKs/Console show JSON views. Profiles should be signed/checked-in as artifacts.

QA-Bot: Tests to add:
- regression suite for top-20 customer prompts across bitwidths
- synthetic NaN injection tests for fast-fallback
- perf microbench for probe latency

Evan: One more interface boundary: should client SDK be able to request "prefer lower quality for cost" and let shim negotiate? e.g., prefer=int8, max_degradation=0.05

Priya: Yeah expose optional client hint header: X-Precision-Preference: prefer=int8;max_deg=0.05. Shim returns selected profile in response metadata.

Marco: Ops note: make sure billing attribution still maps to effective bitpath.

deploy-bot: Canary started on cluster-7 with tag quant-shim-v1 at 1767554540.

Priya: I'll open a brief RFC doc with sketches + telemetry SLOs. Action items: Evan implement caching layer, Lina add calibration metric hooks, Marco coordinate canary with SRE. tagging @SRE for ops SLA concerns.

Evan: I'll pick up caching. ping me if you want a quick pair on probe design.

Lina: I'll draft calibration delta metric and a Jupyter for eval runs.

Priya: Thanks team, will post RFC link once I finish the doc.
